Process-bigraph wrapper for **MCoM 1.0** — the Microbial Community Model, a
scalable box model of phototroph–heterotroph interactions in diverse microbial
communities (Lücken et al., *Geosci. Model Dev.*, 19, 2461–2477, 2026,
[doi:10.5194/gmd-19-2461-2026](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-19-2461-2026)).

> ### ⚠️ This package is a clean-room **reproduction**, not the upstream engine
> MCoM's numerical core is written in **Julia**. This package re-implements
> MCoM's published algorithm in portable Python/NumPy so the model runs with no
> Julia toolchain. The process class is named **`MComReproductionProcess`**; the
> bare name `MComProcess` is reserved for a future bridge to the real Julia
> engine. The reproduction is validated **bit-for-bit** against real MCoM Julia
> output (see [Fidelity](#fidelity) and `REPRODUCTION.md`). Upstream tool:
> <https://github.com/bgc-mod/MCoM> (v1.0.0, MIT).

## What it does

MCoM tracks a microbial community as a system of ODEs in a well-mixed box:

- **Phytoplankton** `P` fix carbon (via a Platt P–I curve or direct rate),
  take up inorganic nitrogen, and exude dissolved organic carbon/nitrogen (DOC,
  DON) — the amount and C:N of the exudate depend on whether growth is light- or
  nutrient-limited.
- **Heterotrophs** `H` consume DOC/DON compounds (each with its own uptake
  kinetics and yield), remineralize inorganic nitrogen `N`, and can produce
  **metabolites** `M` that feed back on phytoplankton mortality (beneficial or
  inhibitory).
- Interactions are specified by scalable **connectivity + rate/release
  matrices**, so the same code covers a single co-culture up to communities of
  hundreds of species.

This wrapper exposes the whole community as one composable process-bigraph
`Process`, with the environmental forcings (light, nutrient supply, temperature)
as input ports a sibling process can drive.

## Installation

```bash
# From PyPI (once published):
pip install viva-mcom
# or with uv:
uv pip install viva-mcom

# For development (editable):
uv venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

> Once installed, the process registers automatically via
> `bigraph_schema.package.discover` — no manual `register_link()` calls are
> needed. (Editable installs may miss distribution-keyed discovery; the
> workspace's `viva_mcom.core.build_core()` registers it explicitly, and a
> regular `uv pip install .` restores auto-discovery.)

## Quick start

```python
from process_bigraph import Composite, gather_emitter_results
from viva_mcom.core import build_core
from viva_mcom.composites.coculture import mcom_coculture

core = build_core()
doc = mcom_coculture(core, t_end=200.0)         # a P–H batch co-culture
sim = Composite({"state": doc}, core=core)
sim.run(200.0)

rows = gather_emitter_results(sim)[("emitter",)]
print(rows[-1]["phytoplankton"], rows[-1]["heterotrophs"], rows[-1]["DIN"])
```

Run the showcase studies (see below) with:

```bash
python workspace/studies/mcom-coculture/sims/run.py
python workspace/studies/mcom-seasonal/sims/run.py
```

## API reference

### `MComReproductionProcess`

| Port | Direction | Schema | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `irradiance` | input | `maybe[float]` | Light forcing; `None` ⇒ use config function |
| `nutrient_supply` | input | `maybe[float]` | External DIN `N_ext` (enters via `D·(N_ext−N)`) |
| `temperature` | input | `maybe[float]` | Accepted; upstream temperature modulation is a stub |
| `phytoplankton` | output | `map[string,float]` | Δ cell density `P0…` [1e6 cells/mL] |
| `heterotrophs` | output | `map[string,float]` | Δ cell density `H0…` |
| `DOC` / `DON` | output | `map[string,float]` | Δ dissolved organic C / N [mM] |
| `metabolites` | output | `map[string,float]` | Δ metabolite level |
| `DIN` | output | `float` | Δ inorganic nitrogen [mM N] |
| `carbon_fixed` / `carbon_lost` | output | `float` | Δ cumulative fixed / respired-and-exported C |

Config: `config_json` (the full MCoM TOML config as JSON), `dt` (integrator
substep, days), `seed`/`source_noise` (only for DIN-supply noise).

Outputs are **per-interval deltas** so they compose additively with sibling
processes; inputs left unwired fall back to the config's own time functions,
reproducing standalone MCoM exactly.

## Architecture

```
viva_mcom/
  engine.py       clean-room MCoM: RHS (mcom_system.jl), AB2 integrator
                  (mcom_numerics.jl), fluctuation grammar (mcom_io.jl)
  config.py       MCoM TOML -> MComParams (deterministic instantiation)
  processes.py    MComReproductionProcess — owns the community, emits deltas
  core.py         build_core() — explicit registration for the dashboard
  composites/     @composite_generator families (dashboard entry points)
```

The `Process` owns the authoritative community state and steps it with MCoM's
own 2nd-order Adams–Bashforth scheme. Upstream Julia → this reproduction mapping:
`mcom_system.jl`→`engine.derivatives`, `mcom_numerics.jl`→`engine.MComEngine.step`,
`mcom_io.jl`→`engine.make_fluctuation_function`, `mcom_generator.jl`→`config.py`.

## Fidelity

`datasets/golden/` holds trajectories produced by the **real MCoM Julia engine**
(from the upstream test suite) with their configs. `tests/test_golden.py`
asserts the reproduction reproduces them to `< 1e-9`. Because those configs are
deterministic, the match is exact. See `REPRODUCTION.md` for the full provenance
and the (RNG-only) divergences.

## Expected outputs

- **mcom-coculture**: phytoplankton blooms (0.01 → ~0.84 @ day 44) then busts;
  the heterotroph rises on the exudate to a peak ~2.39 @ day 50 (lagging the
  bloom ~7 days) — run-mean density > 0.1; inorganic nitrogen is drawn down from
  8.8 mM to a second-half mean ~1.87 mM. Both behaviour tests pass.
- **mcom-seasonal**: a sustained community under 0.1/day dilution — phytoplankton
  oscillates ~0.42–0.89 (2.1× peak/trough) on the annual light cycle without
  washing out; DIN held ~2.1 mM against a 10 mM inflow. Both behaviour tests pass.

## Limitations & assumptions

- **Reproduction, not a bridge.** Runs MCoM's algorithm in NumPy, not the Julia
  binary. Random parameter draws / Dirichlet network splitting are **not**
  reproduced (need Julia's RNG); deterministic configs are exact. Temperature
  rate modulation is a stub upstream and here.
- 0-D well-mixed box (no spatial structure); fixed elemental stoichiometry.
- See the paper's Section 4 for the model's own assumptions and limitations.

## Reference

Lücken, L., Follows, M. J., Bragg, J. G., Lennartz, S. T.: *The microbial
community model MCoM 1.0*, Geosci. Model Dev., 19, 2461–2477, 2026.
Upstream code (MIT): <https://github.com/bgc-mod/MCoM>,
Zenodo <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19108362>.
